title: Qara Qoyunlu
capsule: The Qara Qoyunlu ('Black Sheep Turkomans') was a Turkoman confederation and dynasty that ruled Azerbaijan, Armenia, Iraq, and western Persia from approximately 1374–1375, recovering from Timurid suppression following the Battle of Ankara (1402) under Qara Yusuf, who defeated the Timurids at Nakhchivan in 1406 and seized Tabriz as capital. The confederation peaked under Jahan Shah (r. 1438–1467), who extended Qara Qoyunlu power into the Persian heartland and made Tabriz a court of Persian-Timurid literary culture. In 1467 Jahan Shah was killed at the Battle of Chapakchur fighting Uzun Hasan of the rival Aq Qoyunlu ('White Sheep') confederation; by 1468 Uzun Hasan had conquered all former Qara Qoyunlu territories, extinguishing the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territories in Azerbaijan and Iraq are well attested from contemporary Persian and Ottoman chronicles; peripheral boundaries fluctuated rapidly with nomadic coalition politics and are approximated in cartographic reconstruction.
